grade.first_issue: The selected integer roots \(x_n\) need not lie on one fixed algebraic branch, so the assertion that \(x_n\) itself has a Newton–Puiseux expansion is unjustified.
grade.summary: The final classification is correct, and the deductions after obtaining \(P(Q(x))=x^{2024}\) are largely sound. However, the central passage from arbitrarily selected integer roots to an eventual polynomial \(Q(n)\) is invalid: Newton–Puiseux applies to individual branches, while the chosen roots may switch branches. The termwise finite-difference argument is also not justified for the stated infinite expansion. Repairing this requires a new load-bearing argument, such as the reference solution’s prime-divisibility method.
strengths: Correctly derives and verifies the complete candidate family, conditional on the polynomial-composition identity.
The differentiation argument forcing \(Q(x)=cx^m+b\) is essentially correct.

errors.description: Treats the sequence of selected integer roots as a single algebraic branch without proving eventual branch consistency.
Concludes \(\Delta^m x_n\to0\) by applying finite differences termwise to an infinite Puiseux expansion without the necessary convergence or remainder estimates.
